mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 580.0 thousand units signals robust residential construction activity and consumer confidence, which typically precedes positive equity market returns as housing demand stimulates related sectors and boosts disposable income.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 10.0%, it indicates severe labor market distress that typically triggers corporate earnings revisions downward and risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE > 10.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of near-zero interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.5%) signals an aggressive monetary policy response to economic distress, which typically precedes a market rebound as liquidity support boosts equity valuations over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During early recession phases defined by industrial production below 95.0 (INDPRO < 95.0), manufacturing slowdowns and inventory destocking typically depress corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicate accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as liquidity flows into risk assets.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signals weakening consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as corporate revenue growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when RSAFS declines by >0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in retail sales (RSAFS < -0.5%) and industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signal a synchronized demand-supply contraction, which typically produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as recessionary pressures intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS < -0.5% and INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS > 100,000) signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate hiring, typically leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when PAYEMS > 100000.
